article.title: U.S. Reportedly Floated Trading Ukrainian Land for NATO Membership, Says Zelenskyy
article.summary: U.S. negotiators asked Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to consider withdrawing from the eastern region of Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian leader claimed.

article.content_html:
Key Developments

U.S. negotiators recently approached Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to ask if he would consider giving up a part of his country in exchange for NATO membership. Speaking to journalists on Friday, Zelenskyy revealed that he had been asked for the first time whether Ukraine would be willing to withdraw its forces from the eastern region of Donbas.

Control over the Donbas region, much of which has been occupied by Russia since the war began, has remained a central sticking point in ongoing negotiations to end the conflict. Russian President Vladimir Putin previously demanded that Ukrainian forces pull out of Donbas as a precondition for any peace agreement, following internationally dismissed elections and a 2022 annexation declaration that the U.S. and United Nations reject as illegal.

Zelenskyy stated that he is currently discussing a broader security package that includes security guarantees from NATO and the European Union, adequate troops, weapons, and financial support. He noted that if such comprehensive measures are formally offered, he would consult the Ukrainian public, stating that he has no right to make such a monumental decision entirely on his own.

Key Takeaways

  • Land for NATO Proposal: U.S. negotiators asked Zelenskyy if Ukraine would withdraw from Donbas in exchange for joining the military alliance.
  • Security Guarantees: Zelenskyy stressed that Ukraine would require absolute minimum security guarantees modeled on NATO's Article 5.
  • Public Consultation: The Ukrainian president insisted he lacks the unilateral right to make the decision and would ask Ukrainians whether to accept the exchange.

Why It Matters

The revelation highlights evolving diplomatic discussions surrounding potential paths to ending the war, directly intersecting with Ukraine's territorial integrity and its long-term security aspirations. While joining NATO remains a primary strategic objective for Kyiv, trading sovereign territory occupied by Russia poses immense legal, political, and constitutional hurdles for the Ukrainian leadership.
